text: This closing lesson steps back from mechanics and troubleshooting to place security where it actually sits in a real implementation project — not a task you do once near the end, but a thread running through nearly every phase.

A common mistake on smaller implementations is treating security as a late-stage task, something to configure once the real functional design is finished. In practice, security decisions are embedded in the functional design itself — the business units and ledgers decided during enterprise structure design directly determine the data access sets and business unit contexts from chapter two. Segregation of duties review is far cheaper during role design than after fifty people are already provisioned the wrong combination of roles.

Across the timeline: design phase maps job, abstract, and any needed custom roles against the real org structure. Configuration phase builds out data access sets, business unit assignments, and role mappings. Testing phase verifies all of it, which we'll get to in a moment. Cutover provisions real users, ideally through already-tested role mappings, with the access audit report run as a pre-go-live baseline. And post-go-live means recurring reviews, SoD monitoring, and the troubleshooting method from lesson seventeen as real tickets arrive.

A dedicated security test cycle confirms each role grants exactly the expected function access, no more and no less; that data security policies produce the expected rows; that role mappings autoprovision and self-request correctly; and that no unapproved SoD conflicts exist before go-live. At Castellan Robotics, this ran in parallel with functional user acceptance testing, using the same test accounts — it doesn't need to be a separate, siloed exercise if it's planned for from the start.

This course covered the security model end to end — roles, privileges, data security, provisioning, Financials-specific roles, segregation of duties, reporting, and troubleshooting. The next course in this stage, Oracle Fusion Implementation Lifecycle, zooms out to the full project those security decisions live inside — requirements, configuration, testing, cutover, and go-live support.
